items.prompt: Given an array of points on a plane and k, return the k points closest to the origin.
items.why: k smallest by a key (distance) from an unsorted collection → a size-k max-heap of (-distance, point).

items.prompt: Given an n × n matrix whose rows and columns are each sorted ascending, return the k-th smallest element.
items.why: Rows are already sorted lists, so a heap of row heads walks the smallest k elements in O(k log n) without reading the rest. A size-k heap over all n² elements ignores the order you were given.

items.prompt: Given an array of words, return the k words that appear most often.
items.why: Count with a hash map, then keep the k best by count in a size-k heap. The map is only the first step, and 'k most' decides the pattern.

items.prompt: Numbers arrive one at a time. After each one, return the median of the numbers seen so far.
items.why: The median's position (half the count) moves as numbers arrive. A fixed-size k heap can't follow it, so balance two halves instead.

items.prompt: Given ropes of different lengths, join them all into one rope. Joining two ropes costs the sum of their lengths. Return the minimum total cost.
items.why: Repeatedly take the two smallest and push the result back → a min-heap with repeated extraction (the Top K chapter's heap greedy).

items.prompt: Given an array and k, return the largest sum of any k consecutive elements.
items.why: 'Consecutive' means a contiguous window, not the k largest anywhere → a fixed sliding window with a running sum.

items.prompt: Given an array of n numbers in the range 1..n, some missing and some repeated, return the first k missing positive numbers.
items.why: Values in 1..n that should sit at their own index → cyclic sort, then read off the misplaced slots. The k only limits how many you report.

items.prompt: Remove exactly k elements from an array so that the number of distinct elements left is as large as possible. Return that number.
items.why: Count, then fix the duplicated values with the smallest counts first while the budget lasts → a min-heap keyed by frequency.
